# TyraX game project - instructions for AI assistants

This is a **PlayStation 2 game generated by the TyraX editor**. The editor owns
the data model and regenerates the game's C++ from it on every build; the game
builds with native PS2DEV/OpenVCL by default and runs in PCSX2. Docker is an optional fallback.

## TyraX2 custom-code contract

[TyraX2 source documentation](https://github.com/doctorspider42/tyraX/blob/main/docs/tyrax2.md) describes the default-off frame pipeline.
Ordinary renderer APIs supply ordering fences; do not add an unconditional
wait to every custom node/script. Raw DMA/GS writes and CPU GPU readbacks are
not automatically recorded. Use `Tyra::frameSendPacket` from
`renderer/core/paths/path1/frame_submission.hpp` for custom packets, or retain
the queue/channel completion and source-ownership contract; drain
`Tyra::Vif1Queue` before a foreign direct VIF1 send. DMA completion alone does
not release a GS texture reader.

Call `RendererCore::setFramePipeline(bool)` only between frames;
`getFramePipeline()` returns the request, not actual overlap in compatibility
modes. Before a between-frame CPU GPU readback, call
`renderer.core.synchronizeFrame()` (the generated debugger does). During
recording, `sync.align3D()` / `sync.align2D()` may only record ordering barriers,
so neither they nor `synchronizeFrame()` are a general mid-recording readback
or resource-destruction recipe. Keep referenced buffers and VRAM alive until
their actual readers complete.

## Rules that prevent lost work

1. **Never edit** editor-owned files: everything under `src/gen/` and
   `vugen/`, all `*.gen.cpp`/`*.gen.hpp`, `inc/scene_data.hpp`,
   `inc/terrain_config.hpp` (first line `Generated by TyraX. Do not edit -
   regenerated on every build`), and the marker-less but always rewritten
   `src/main.cpp`, `Makefile`, `docker-compose.yml`,
   `.vscode/c_cpp_properties.json`. Change the project data instead. Build
   flags go in the project preferences (`cppStandard`, `extraCompilerFlags`,
   `extraLinkerFlags`) or in a `user.mk` beside the Makefile, which is yours
   and which the Makefile includes last.
2. Files marked `Delete this line to take ownership` (`src/terrain_game.cpp`,
   `inc/terrain_game.hpp`, `inc/controls.hpp`, `inc/scripts/script.hpp`,
   `inc/scripts/flow_nodes.hpp`) are regenerated only while the marker is
   intact; delete the marker line before hand-editing them (they then stop
   receiving editor updates). The game runtime beyond `terrain_game.cpp` is
   editor-owned in `src/gen/game_*.gen.cpp` + `inc/game_runtime.gen.hpp`; an
   owned `terrain_game.cpp` must keep `#include "game_runtime.gen.hpp"`.
3. Game/scene data lives in `<name>.tyra` + `objects/<id>.json` (+
   `terrain-*.heights`), not in C++. `<name>.history` is disposable editor
   state. Assets live under `res/`.
4. A scene's **terrain is optional** (`"terrain": { ..., "enabled": false }`).
   With it removed the scene has no ground and the game has **no floor**: the
   player, physics bodies and particles rest on the geometry the scene places
   and fall through the void anywhere else, a Player/spawn point starts at its
   own Y, and navigation AI has nothing to walk on. The scene's width/depth
   still bound the world.

## Where your code goes

- **Scripts**: `src/scripts/*.cpp`. Object scripts derive from `ObjectScript`
  (`onStart`/`onUpdate`/`onUsed`, `self`), are registered with
  `TYRA_OBJECT_SCRIPT(Name);` inside the project namespace and attached in
  Properties > Scripts; global scripts derive from `Script` (`init`/`update`)
  and register with `TYRA_SCRIPT(Ns::Name);` (see
  `src/scripts/example_interaction.cpp`). API: `inc/scripts/script.hpp`,
  which includes the `tyrax::` script API (`inc/tyrax/tyrax.hpp`: what every
  flow node does - `object.moveBy`, `tyrax::raycast`, `tyrax::playSound`,
  `tyrax::sendEvent` ... - plus vectors, easing, random, timers) and the
  project's names as typed constants (`inc/tyrax/names.gen.hpp`:
  `tyrax::Sounds::X`, `tyrax::Objects::<Scene>::X`). Prefer it over raw
  `ScriptContext` fields; an object script's own object is `object`.
  Values a designer should tune per object are members marked
  `[[tyra::prop]]` (options `min`, `max`, `tooltip`, `header`,
  `options = "A|B"`, `color`): they appear in Properties > Scripts and are
  stored per object as `"scriptProps"` in its JSON. Callbacks beyond
  onStart/onUpdate/onUsed: onLateUpdate, onEvent, onPlayerEnter/Exit (Area
  objects), onAnimationFinished, onActivated/Deactivated, onSceneEnd.
  `tyrax::getScript<T>(obj)` / `findScript<T>()` reach other scripts;
  `TYRA_SCRIPT_METHOD(Class, method);` makes a method callable from the flow
  graph's *Call Script* node (str "Class.method").
- **Script extensions**: `src/extensions/<name>/` (`extension.json`, scripts
  wrapped in `TYRAX_NAMESPACE_BEGIN`/`TYRAX_NAMESPACE_END`, `flow-nodes/`
  with `include =` for a node's C++). Compiled like src/scripts; install with
  `tyrax-editor --install-extension <projectDir> <folder>`.
- **Custom flow nodes**: `flow-nodes/*.flownode` (header + `---` + C++ body;
  `call = fn` bodies live in `inc/scripts/flow_nodes.hpp`).
- **Custom screen effects**: `screen-effects/*.screenfx`.
- **Menu stylesheets**: `menu-styles/*.menustyle` - CSS-shaped, what a menu
  looks like; a menu names one in its `"style"` key ("" = the Classic look).
  Selectors are `panel`/`title`/`list`/`row`/`value`/`description`/`hint`/
  `marker`, with `row:selected` / `row:disabled` states, `row.myclass` classes
  and `menu#name` scopes; `@transition` and `@animate` add motion. Everything
  static is baked at build time, so gradients, frames, shadows and outlines cost
  the console nothing while each painted row STATE costs one baked cell - the
  Menu Editor prints the VRAM. A baked gradient cannot move: use
  `background-anim` (a scrolling tile or a frame strip) for that.

## Flow graphs (game logic)

Every scene object owns a flow graph (in its `objects/<id>.json`), compiled to
`src/gen/flow_graph.gen.cpp` at build. Graph JSON:
`{"nodes":[{"id":1,"type":"OnStart","pos":[0,0],"str":"","num":[0,0,0,0]}],`
`"links":[{"from":1,"to":2,"kind":"exec"}]}` with link kinds
`exec`/`object`/`pos`/`bool`/`text`/`number`; an exec link may add `"pin"`
(which labeled exec input fires, e.g. Set Int 1=add) and `"fpin"` (which
labeled output it leaves, e.g. Branch 0=true/1=false). `type` is the catalog id
from `--list-nodes`. Triggers have the exec output; actions
have only an exec input (wire each action from the trigger; Delay's "after"
output sequences over time). Object params resolve link → `str` name → self;
logic gates are pure and bridge back to exec via On Condition (rising edge).
Any text may contain `{{cross}}` (a pad-button glyph) or `{{action:jump}}` (the
glyph of whatever that action is bound to) - see docs/text-icons.md.
For buttons prefer the **On Action** trigger (`str` = an input-action name from
the project's Input Map, e.g. `jump` / `sprint`): it follows the current
binding, including a preset switch and the player's own in-game rebind.
`On Button` (raw pad button) and `On Key` (raw USB keyboard key) bypass that on
purpose - use them only for a fixed debug key.

## The TyraX editor CLI (use it - it validates)

The editor executable on this machine: `{TYRAX_EXE}`

- `--dump <projectDir>` - JSON summary (scenes, objects, every referencable name)
- `--list-nodes <projectDir>` - full flow-node catalog + JSON schema
- `--dump-graph <projectDir> <object> [scene]` - one object's graph
- `--apply-graph <projectDir> <object> <graph.json> [scene] [--append]` -
  validate + write a graph
- `--ai-graph <projectDir> <object> <prompt|file> [scene] [--backend claude|copilot|openai] [--model m] [--thinking]` - AI graph generation
- `--refresh-gen <projectDir>` - regenerate game sources without building
  (fast codegen check; dangling references appear as `unknown ...` comments in
  `flow_graph.gen.cpp`)
- `--build <projectDir> [--run | --run-ps2 [ip]] [--rebuild] [--docker]` -
  full native build (+ PCSX2 launch / real-PS2 deploy); `--docker` selects the
  fallback
- `--debug-run <projectDir> [--no-build] [--rebuild] [--enable]` - script debugger: build,
  run in PCSX2 and serve GDB (VS Code F5 attaches); `--debug-serve <projectDir>
  [--pine-slot N]` serves a game launched elsewhere (docs/script-debugger.md)
- `--list-extensions <projectDir>`, `--new-extension <projectDir> <name>`,
  `--install-extension <projectDir> <folder>` - script extensions in
  `src/extensions`
- `--new <name> <parentDir> [w] [d] [empty|fpp|thirdperson] [unitsPerMeter] [--no-terrain]` - create a project
- `--resave <projectDir>` - load + save with validation
- `--migrate <projectDir>` - back up into `_backup/` and apply pending format
  migrations; commands that write the project refuse until this has run
- `--bake-status <projectDir>` - read-only freshness of every bake cache (GI,
  baked shadows, pre-lit, model AO); exit 3 = something is stale
- `--bake-gi <projectDir> [--gpu]` - bake global illumination + light probes
  into `.res-baked/gi/`
- `--bake-shadows <projectDir>` - bake the static shadow decals into
  `.res-baked/shadow/` (docs/shadows.md)
- `--bake-prelit <projectDir> [sceneName]` - re-bake every stale pre-lit
  object, then save + regenerate (a second run bakes nothing)
- GI, shadow and pre-lit bakes are explicit: a build only READS their caches
  (a stale one silently falls back to unbaked lighting) unless the project set
  `giAutoBake` / `bakedShadowAutoBake` / `prelitAutoBake`
- `--bake-model-ao <projectDir> [--texbake]` - bake every `.obj` model's own
  AO into `.res-baked/modelao/` and report skips (a build does it too)
- `--bake-particles <projectDir>` - re-bake the particle library's generated
  textures (docs/particles.md)
- `--import-model <projectDir> <model> [--split none|top|mesh] [--pivot keep|bottom|center] [--keep f] [--max-texture px] [--animated] [--no-static] [--textures dir] [--name stem] [--dry-run]` -
  the editor's single model importer, headless: `.obj`/`.glb`/`.fbx` -> static
  `.obj` + `.mtl` + PNGs, and with `--animated` the `.glb`/`.fbx` + `.mtl` too
  (a Model object draws the `.obj`, an Animated model object the `.glb`/`.fbx`).
  Does not place objects
- `--search-docs "<terms>" [page]` - search the editor's built-in docs (the
  `docs/<page>.md` cited here are not in the project; `page` = name without
  `.md`)
- `--add-ai-support <projectDir> [claude] [codex] [copilot]` - reinstall these
  guides
- `--pad <projectDir> "<script>"` - drive the RUNNING debug game's controller
  through `bin/livepad.bin` (no window focus needed; *Remote Pad* preference,
  on by default): `press cross [s]`, `hold up`, `release all`,
  `stick l|r <x> <y>` (-127..127), `wait <s>`, `neutral`, `pad 1|2`, separated
  by `;`. Walkers read the analog sticks, not the D-pad; a `hold` needs a
  `wait` after it (the driver releases the pad on exit). On Windows check its
  stderr/exit code first: `Start-Process -ArgumentList` does not quote the
  script (pass it from a `.ps1` as a literal).
- `--record <projectDir> <out.tyrarep> [--pad "<script>"] [--seconds N]` and
  `--replay <projectDir> <file.tyrarep>` - record every frame of input, then
  build, run and perform it again. **Replay exit 0 = reproduced exactly, 3 =
  diverged, 1 = could not run** - a regression test for a play session. Needs
  the *Input recorder* preference (OFF by default). See docs/input-replay.md.
- `--capture-frame <projectDir> [-o out.png] [--alpha a.png] [--timeout s]` -
  the running debug game photographs its own frame buffer (Live Debugger on;
  works over ps2link too); default `screenshots/frame-cli.png`.
- `--profile-frame <projectDir> [-o report.csv]` - one synchronized render-cost
  pass from the running debug game (Live Debugger on; waits up to 45 s; it
  drains VU/GS between draws, so use ordinary FPS for throughput). GUI twin:
  Debugger > Render cost.

## Building and debugging

The first native build provisions and verifies the toolchain automatically; output lands in
`bin/<name>.elf`. The running game's log is `bin/log.txt`; `TYRA_ASSERT`
failures print a block delimited by `======= TYRA =======` ...
`================` naming the file/line (a `Non-fatal` header = the game
recovered). Both build profiles write the log; under ps2link it goes to the
editor's Output panel and `logs/` instead. Verify changes with
`--refresh-gen` + diff first, then `--build`.

## VU programs (the vector units)

A project can replace the microprogram **VU1** runs over every vertex, and can
run compute batches on **VU0** - both in ordinary C++, no assembly.

- `src/vu/*.cpp` = a `vu::Program` (a per-vertex effect: cell shading, a
  palette, a wobble, vertex snapping). `src/vu0/*.cpp` = a `vu::Kernel` (N
  quadwords in, N out).
- **The C++ does not run on the PS2.** It runs on the build machine once, and
  every operation you write APPENDS an instruction - the file is a description
  of a microprogram, not the microprogram's body.
- A program replaces a **material class**, not an object, so it draws every mesh
  of that class; per-mesh strength comes from four floats (`c.params`). A
  program that MOVES geometry must claim every class, or an object's several
  passes separate.
- **Never divide** (`divQ`/`rsqrtQ`) inside a **VU1** body: it lands in the
  perspective divide's latency window and vertices come out wrong on hardware
  while the host simulator shows nothing. A **VU0 kernel** may divide freely -
  nothing else there owns Q. Four scratch registers on both.
- VU0 has **no cross-element reduction** - a kernel computes the terms, the CPU
  folds them (find the minimum in a loop after `run()`), and `run()` blocks the
  EE while it works.
- `vugen/vushader.hpp` is the reference; `Tools > VU Programs` holds the
  micro-memory budget (2042 slots for the whole resident set - overrunning it
  hangs the frame in a release build).

## VS Code

The TyraX extension (`.flownode`/`.screenfx`/`.menustyle` highlighting +
validation) is
recommended via `.vscode/extensions.json`; `.vscode/c_cpp_properties.json`
(PS2 include paths for IntelliSense) is regenerated by the editor.
